banner.selfcheckAbnormal: Self-check found problems: {{problems}}. This is not "no alerts" — you may not receive alerts at all.

warroom.emptyReason: All rules are executing normally; nothing needs attention right now
warroom.emptyReasonRisk: Careful: {{count}} rule(s) are failing to execute — an empty list does not mean the system is healthy
warroom.silentTitle: Silent failure: data source stopped reporting
warroom.silentBody: {{names}} is reachable but has returned no data for over 30 minutes. Rules on it are blind — this is not "no alerts".
warroom.allClearReason: The detection path is intact: data sources are reachable and every rule is running. Right now “no alerts” really does mean “nothing is wrong”.
warroom.emptyTitleRisk: No alerts — but the detection path has gaps

incidents.emptyReason: Try another status filter, or check whether rules are executing normally
incidents.chainNone: No decision chain for this incident (retention expired, or it came from an inbound webhook)
incidents.trendLabel: Hits over the last {{count}} cycles of the owning rule
incidents.sampleNone: No sample was kept for this incident
incidents.similarNone: First occurrence of this fingerprint — no history to compare against

verdict.noRoute: No route matched — nobody will be notified

rules.scopeHint: Phase one covers the four log-side detections; metric alerting stays with Nightingale and is not duplicated here
rules.emptyReason: Connect a log data source first, then create rules by scenario — or import from the legacy alerting system

form.title: New rule
form.desc: Dry-run before saving: finding a broken query only at the next schedule tick costs too much
form.name: Rule name
form.queryHint: LogQL for Loki; query string or raw DSL (starting with {) for ES. Sent verbatim — the platform never rewrites it
form.forHint: One blip should not page anyone
form.willFire: Groups that would fire at this threshold: {{groups}}
form.willFireNone: No group would fire at this threshold

rules.deleteHint: The rule stops running; past incidents are kept. This cannot be undone.
rules.rawEditHint: It was not created from a template, so there are no parameters to prefill. Edit its query with “Manual rule”, or delete it and recreate it from a template.
rules.metricsHint: Exposes this rule's hit count, run count and last-run time on /metrics
rules.metricsLabelsHint: Attached to every metric of this rule, e.g. project=G32. job / instance are reserved by Prometheus and not allowed

backtest.paramsHint: Replay a rule draft over historical data. No notifications, no incidents.
backtest.draftHint: What you want to change it to
backtest.idle: No backtest yet. Fill in the parameters on the left — worth running before changing any threshold.
backtest.running: Running… (larger ranges take longer; 30 days is about a minute)
backtest.missedWarning: These groups would no longer fire under the draft — confirm each one is not a missed detection:
backtest.missedNone: Every group the baseline fired on is still covered by the draft
backtest.queryErrors: {{count}} window(s) failed to query during the replay (historical data may have retention gaps). The conclusion is based on incomplete data.

silences.hint: A silence suppresses notification, not detection: incidents are still recorded, and anything still unresolved when the window ends is notified again
silences.emptyReason: Nothing is silenced — every incident is notified through its route
silences.formDesc: A silence must expire — a permanent one is pretending nothing is wrong, and nobody comes back to remove it
silences.reasonHint: Say why — whoever takes over the shift will read this

noise.hint: The loop: mark false positives → noise ranking → tuning advice → verify by backtest → adopt. Advice is input for a human decision; the system never changes a threshold on its own.
noise.emptyTitle: No incidents in the last 7 days
noise.emptyReason: No incidents means no noise data. If a rule should have fired but did not, check rule health in self-check first

datasources.hint: Phase one supports Loki / Elasticsearch / OpenSearch; metric sources come in phase two
datasources.emptyReason: Detection rules need a data source; connect a Loki or Elasticsearch first
datasources.formDesc: Credentials are encrypted at rest and never returned by any endpoint — not even the ciphertext
datasources.orgIdHint: Loki's X-Scope-OrgID; leave empty for single-tenant deployments
datasources.indexPatternHint: e.g. biz-log-*. Leave empty to search all indices
datasources.apiKeyHint: ES 8 accepts an API key instead of username/password

notifiers.hint: Phase one supports Feishu and generic webhooks; other channels use the same adapter interface
notifiers.testOk: Test message delivered (confirmed by the receiver)
notifiers.emptyReason: Without a notifier, incidents are only recorded — nobody is told
notifiers.secretHintFeishu: Signature secret of the Feishu bot
notifiers.secretHintWebhook: Lets the receiver verify the signature — strongly recommended

routes.emptyReason: Without a route nobody gets notified. There must be at least a fallback route
routes.fallbackProtected: The fallback route cannot be deleted: without it, unmatched incidents vanish silently
routes.noCondition: No condition (matches everything not caught above)
routes.simulateHint: Feed it a set of labels and see which branch it takes and who gets notified — no need to wait for a real alert to find out the route is wrong.
routes.willNotNotify: Nobody would be notified for this incident
routes.formDesc: Matched top-down, first match wins. Tick “keep matching” to let one alert take several branches.
routes.repeatHelp: How often to re-notify for the same incident; 0 means notify once

selfcheck.failed: The self-check endpoint itself failed: {{error}}. The backend or database has a problem, so no "everything is fine" conclusion can be trusted right now.
selfcheck.healthy: Detection path is intact — "no alerts" can be read as "nothing is wrong"
selfcheck.unhealthy: Detection path has gaps — "no alerts" cannot be read as "nothing is wrong"
selfcheck.silentDetailHint: No data returned for over 30 minutes; rules on it are blind

audit.emptyReason: Every write is recorded; an empty list means nothing has been changed yet

mcp.hint: Over MCP, an AI can read rules, incidents, decision chains and self-check, and run read-only dry runs. No write tools in phase one — creating rules, changing thresholds and silencing are all withheld, for the same reason the system never changes a threshold on its own: when it goes wrong, nobody can say who decided it.
mcp.issuedTitle: This token is shown only once — save it now
mcp.issuedHint: If lost, revoke and create a new one: only a hash is stored, no endpoint can return the plaintext.
mcp.emptyReason: An AI needs a token to connect; issue one per consumer so they can be revoked individually
mcp.toolsHint: 10 read-only tools. why_not_fired is the one for chasing missing alerts: give it a rule ID and it tells you which step of the decision chain it stopped at — no hits / not sustained long enough / inhibited / silenced / no route matched / the rule itself is erroring.
mcp.formDesc: One token per consumer, so it can be revoked and traced individually
mcp.consumerHint: Say who uses it, e.g. claude-code, ai-copilot

error.noTenant: This account has no tenant membership
error.fallbackProtected: The fallback route cannot be deleted
error.noEndTime: A silence must have an end time
error.unsupportedKind: This rule type is not implemented in phase one
error.unsupportedType: This data source type is not implemented in phase one

perm.deniedTitle: You don’t have access to this page
perm.deniedReason: It’s hidden from the menu because your account is missing the permission below. Send it to an administrator to request access.
perm.needCode: Requires permission: {{code}}. Send this code to an administrator to request access.
perm.fillRequired: Fill in the required fields first
perm.fallbackKeep: The fallback route cannot be deleted — without it some alerts would have nowhere to go

import.title: Import rules from the legacy alerting system
import.desc: Preflight first, then apply. Preflight only computes — it shows how each rule translates and what needs your attention.
import.pasteHint: Paste the JSON exported from the legacy system (an array of rules)
import.notArray: The top level must be an array of rules, e.g. [{...},{...}]
import.pickNone: Select the rules to import first
import.pickHint: Only “ready” rules are pre-selected; review the notes before selecting the others

tpl.title: Create from scenario
tpl.desc: Pick a scenario and answer a few questions — the query is generated for you.
tpl.previewFirst: Generate the query first to see what it produces
tpl.name: Rule name
tpl.intervalHelp: How often to run the query
tpl.forPeriodsHelp: How many times in a row before alerting — one blip should not page anyone

tplPage.hint: Start from a scenario: answer a few questions and the LogQL, field extraction and grouping are generated for you. For anything the templates do not cover, use “Manual rule”.
tplPage.emptyReason: Templates are built into the platform; an empty list usually means a backend version mismatch.

error_code.name: Error-code alerts
error_code.when: Alert when service logs contain ERROR with a business error code — while a known set of codes should never page anyone

namespaces.label: Namespaces
namespaces.help: Namespaces to watch; you can add several

container_include.label: Only these containers
container_include.help: Regex. Leave empty for every container in the namespace

container_exclude.label: Exclude these containers
container_exclude.help: Regex. Leave empty to exclude none

ignore_codes.label: Codes that should not alert
ignore_codes.help: These are normal business responses. They are written straight into the query as an exclusion

log_heartbeat.name: Log gone quiet (heartbeat)
log_heartbeat.when: A group of services should keep emitting a certain log line — silence for a while means it stopped working

log_pattern.label: Log signature
log_pattern.help: What the healthy log line looks like

expected_containers.label: Containers expected to run
expected_containers.help: ⚠️ List them all. A container you leave out will never alert even if it goes completely silent — groups come from the data, and a container with zero log lines never appears in the result

latency_threshold.name: Latency over threshold
latency_threshold.when: Pull a duration out of the logs and alert when it exceeds a threshold

log_pattern.label: Log signature
log_pattern.help: Narrow down to these lines first

cost_pattern.label: Regex that captures the duration
cost_pattern.help: The capture group holds the number itself

agg.label: Aggregation
agg.help: p50 / p95 / p99 / max / avg. Prefer p95 over max — one occasional slow call is not a problem

users.hint: Local accounts. The role decides what they can see and change.
users.createDesc: The new account is attached to the current tenant and can sign in right away.
users.notLocal: This account comes from an external identity provider; its password is not held here
users.needFields: Username, password (8+ chars) and role are all required
users.resetPwDesc: The new password takes effect immediately.
users.deleteHint: The account is soft-deleted and audit history is kept. The same username can be created again later.
users.emptyReason: At least one administrator is needed, otherwise nobody can maintain rules and data sources.
users.rolesHint: Roles are built in and their permissions are defined by the platform. Changing a role’s scope means changing the permission map in code.

brief.verdictQuietButGaps: No alerts — but the detection path has gaps.
brief.subtitle: {{rules}} of {{total}} rules watching {{sources}} of {{allSources}} data sources.
brief.deliveryFailed: These may never have reached anyone
brief.noneReason: Every source is reachable and every rule is running. Right now “no alerts” really does mean “nothing is wrong”.
brief.noneButGaps: But the detection path has {{count}} gaps, so this quiet proves nothing.

trend.allZero: No hits at all in this window — the query may be failing; check run history on the Rules page

series.title: Alert volume
series.zero: No new alerts in this time range
series.aria: Alert volume over time, {{total}} total, up to {{peak}} at a single point

explore.intro: Search raw logs through the same path the rules use. It answers "why didn't this alert" — same data source, same query syntax, so what you see here is what the rule sees.
explore.exprPlaceholder: LogQL for Loki, query string for ES
explore.truncated: Truncated — there are more matches than shown
explore.emptyTitle: No matching logs in this time range
explore.emptyReason: The query itself succeeded. There may genuinely be none, or the query or time range may be off.
explore.startTitle: Pick a data source to start
explore.startReason: Most often used to confirm why a rule didn't match: search here first to see whether the logs arrived at all, and what they look like.

report.noNotifiers: No notifiers configured yet — add one under Notifiers first
report.needNotifier: Enabling the report requires at least one delivery channel, otherwise it can never be sent
report.neverSent: The report is enabled but has never been sent. If the send time has passed and nothing arrived, use "Send now" to check the channels.
report.loadError: Failed to load the report settings

license.capFromCE: Not activated — these are the built-in community limits.
license.capFromLicense: These limits come from your license.
license.fNotImplemented: licensed, not yet implemented in this version
license.fingerprintHint: Send this full string when requesting a license. It is derived from the database and changes if the database is moved or the deployment is copied.
license.fingerprintError: Could not compute the fingerprint (usually the database is unreachable). This does not mean there is no fingerprint.
license.tokenPlaceholder: Paste the whole activation code here
license.graceBanner: The license has expired and is in its grace period. {{days}} days until the system becomes read-only. Please renew.
license.fingerprintBanner: The install fingerprint does not match the license (usually after moving the database or copying the deployment). The system becomes read-only in {{days}} days — contact us to re-issue.
license.expiredBanner: The license has expired and the system is read-only. It recovers immediately on renewal.
license.lapsedBanner: The license has been lapsed for more than {{days}} days. Please contact us.
license.notLicensedBanner: This license does not include this product. Please check that you have the right activation code.
license.remindBanner: The license expires in {{days}} days, followed by a {{grace}}-day grace period.
license.unknownStatus: Unrecognised license status ({{status}}). This usually means the backend is newer than the frontend — please upgrade the frontend.

statusHint.active: The license is valid; all purchased features are available.
statusHint.grace: The license has expired but is still within its grace period; features keep working.
statusHint.expired: The license expired and the grace period is over — the system is read-only.
statusHint.lapsed: The license has been lapsed for a long time. Please contact us.
statusHint.finger_mismat: The install fingerprint does not match the license — usually after moving the database or copying this deployment.
statusHint.not_activated: Community edition. This is a normal state, not a fault; enterprise features are not enabled.
statusHint.not_licensed: This license does not include this product.

license.lockedNeedsLicense: This is an enterprise feature and your current license does not include it. The feature itself is ready — activating the right license enables it immediately, no version upgrade needed.
license.lockedNotImplemented: Your license already includes this feature, but this version has not implemented it yet. Upgrading to a version that supports it is enough — no new purchase needed.
license.lockedWhere: The install fingerprint and the activation form are on the License page in the sidebar.

msgtpl.intro: What an alert looks like when it arrives is decided here. ⚠️ A broken template will not stop alerts from being sent — the system falls back to the built-in wording and appends a note.
msgtpl.builtinReadonly: Built-in templates are the fallback used when rendering fails, so they cannot be edited or deleted. Copy one to make changes.
msgtpl.name: Name
msgtpl.channelHint: Leave empty for any channel. Feishu uses cards and webhook takes arbitrary JSON — split them when the structure differs.
msgtpl.title: Title template
msgtpl.needNameBody: Name and body template are both required
msgtpl.varsHint: Click to insert into the body.
msgtpl.varsExtra: Business fields defined by a rule's extract_fields can be used directly under the names you gave them. On a name clash: extracted fields > labels > built-ins.
msgtpl.emptyReason: The built-in templates should be here — if none show up, migration 015 may not have run.

sso.intro: Connect any OIDC identity provider (Azure AD, Keycloak, Okta, in-house). Endpoints and claim names are all configurable — every provider names things differently, and hard-coding one set means the second one fails with "Claim not found".
sso.loadError: Failed to load the SSO settings
sso.saved: Saved. Changes take effect immediately, no restart needed.
sso.callbackHint: Paste this exactly into your provider's application settings. One character off (a missing port, http vs https) and it is rejected — and the provider only says "redirect_uri mismatch" without telling you what differs.
sso.autoDiscoverHint: Fetched from the issuer's /.well-known/openid-configuration. Some providers do not publish it, or publish endpoints that differ from the real ones — turn this off and fill them in.
sso.secretSetHint: Set. Leave empty to keep it unchanged.
sso.secretUnsetHint: Not set. Public (PKCE) clients may leave it empty.
sso.claimSourceHint: 🔴 Defaults to both. Some providers put name and email only in userinfo, not in the id_token — reading just one source fails with "Claim not found" while the provider side looks perfectly fine.
sso.usernameClaimHint: The local account name comes from this. On a failed sign-in, the error lists the claims the provider actually sent.
sso.groupsClaimHint: Nested paths work, e.g. Keycloak's realm_access.roles. A single group sent as a plain string is also accepted.
sso.jitHint: When off, people who exist in the provider but not here cannot sign in — an admin has to create the account first.
sso.defaultRoleHint: 🔴 Cannot be admin. Making admin the default means anyone in the identity provider becomes an administrator here after a single sign-in.
sso.roleMappingHint: One per line, e.g. ops-admin=rule_admin. Re-applied on every sign-in — that is the only way someone removed from a group in the provider actually loses access here.
